name: Modafinil
summary: Modafinil is a wake-promoting prescription medication used in the United States for excessive sleepiness associated with narcolepsy, obstructive sleep apnea, and shift work disorder. This profile remains research-only while indication-specific efficacy, serious-rash and hypersensitivity, psychiatric, cardiovascular, interaction, abuse/dependence, and regulatory evidence is assembled and reviewed.
description: Canonical modafinil entity for evidence and safety integration. Publication remains held until narcolepsy, obstructive-sleep-apnea, and shift-work evidence is kept indication-specific and serious-rash, psychiatric, cardiovascular, reproductive-interaction, controlled-substance, and regulatory provenance passes the site’s review gates.
primary_effects_or_targets: wake-promoting central nervous system activity; dopamine-transporter-related signaling
safety_notes: Current U.S. prescribing information warns about serious rash including Stevens-Johnson syndrome, angioedema/anaphylaxis and multi-organ hypersensitivity, persistent sleepiness, psychiatric symptoms, and cardiovascular events. Modafinil can reduce steroidal-contraceptive effectiveness during treatment and for one month after discontinuation, and it is a Schedule IV controlled substance. In obstructive sleep apnea it treats excessive sleepiness, not the underlying obstruction. This summary is not exhaustive; consult current product-specific prescribing information.
